title: Employment Preference for Military Personnel
lastAction: Re-ref Com On Commerce and Economic Development
aiSummary: This bill expands North Carolina's employment preference policy for military personnel by removing the requirement that service occur during wartime and extending preference to active duty service members, Armed Forces Reserve members, and their spouses and dependents. The expanded preference applies to state job applications, hirings, promotions, reassignments, and transfers.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this bill recognizes military service more broadly, as service members contribute to national defense during both peacetime and wartime. They contend the expansion helps military families and active duty personnel transition to civilian employment, and that spouses and dependents of service members deserve consideration for supporting military families' sacrifices and relocations.
aiConArguments: Opponents may argue that removing wartime requirements dilutes the preference intended for those who served during actual conflicts, and that extending preference to spouses and dependents of all active duty members—rather than only those disabled or killed—could limit job opportunities for non-military applicants. They may also question whether state employment preferences should apply to those still on active duty when federal law already restricts off-duty employment.
